A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Membership Privacy Risks of Sharpness Aware Minimization. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original membership-attack experiments, memorization and influence analyses, synthetic experiments, Hessian measurements, and architecture comparisons.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds ASAM/GSAM comparisons, online/offline shadow-model attacks, and ROC results.

M1.justification: The SAM objective, proposed Sharp objective, and influence-entropy grouping procedure are retained. ASAM/GSAM and LiRA/RMIA are added comparison methods; minimum-G interpolation is introduced as a theoretical model, without a documented change to the experimental algorithms.

E1.justification: The five benchmark datasets and synthetic classification task remain. v4 extends attacker-information scenarios to online shadow attacks using IN/OUT references and offline attacks using OUT-only references, without adding a data domain or prediction task.

E2.justification: v4 adds evaluated LiRA and RMIA attacks in online and offline modes, plus ASAM and GSAM optimizer comparisons on four datasets. The earlier direct-attack methods remain. Sharp's four non-EyePacs comparisons move to Table 3, while its EyePacs comparison is removed.

E3.justification: New shadow-model experiments use 256 random half-split models, with one target and the others serving as references. v4 specifies dataset-dependent sample pools and adds AUC, TPR at 0.1% FPR, and ROC evaluation. These are additional protocols; the retained direct-attack training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds a threshold-wide check of the privacy ordering, and Section 3 newly reports high-confidence nonmember errors among both correctly and incorrectly classified examples. The earlier memorization, influence, synthetic, Hessian, and architecture analyses remain.

E5.justification: v4 reports averaging online shadow-attack results over ten attack splits, but removes v3's statement that Table 1 averages five randomized attack-data splits. These concern different experiments and do not establish increased repetitions of retained results. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds optimizer results, online/offline attack results, and ROC findings while retaining the earlier SAM/SGD direct-attack, Hessian, and architecture values. New online CIFAR-100 LiRA AUC is 92.6% for SGD and 93.7% for SAM; leakage is not uniformly higher for SAM, as Texas-100 online RMIA TPR at 0.1% FPR is 2.9% versus 2.8%. Shadow results use different splits from Table 1. Sharp's EyePacs results disappear.

T1.justification: v4 introduces Gaussian regression, minimum-G interpolation with G = I + eta Sigma, new assumptions, and variance, confidence-attack, likelihood-ratio, and sample-adaptive ROC arguments. v3's minority-alignment generalization theorem survives as Theorem 4 in Appendix B with proofs in C.3. Its minority-alignment privacy theorem and beta-stability assumption are removed.

C1.justification: The central empirical privacy/generalization claim remains, but v4 makes variance shrinkage, strict confidence/LR attack advantages, and ROC dominance central theoretical contributions. v3 instead emphasized minority alignment jointly improving generalization and increasing leakage. v4 also emphasizes feature-diversity bias and drops the contribution claiming release of memorization and influence scores.

C2.justification: v4 adds a mechanism connecting majority-feature dependence to extreme nonmember confidence and explaining SAM's leakage through variance suppression and broader feature reliance. Figure 2's caption no longer labels SGD's highly memorized points as noise. Appendix F also explains online/offline attack-ranking differences through architecture and training choices.

D1.justification: v4 adds a shadow-training code reference, reference-model construction details, sample-pool sizes, RMIA gamma = 1, and auxiliary-sample selection instructions. Existing architectures, training schedules, preprocessing, Sharp hyperparameters, and entropy-bucket construction are retained. These additions document the new experiments.

R1.justification: v4 substantially revises positioning by acknowledging earlier privacy–utility tradeoffs, introducing the feature-diversity versus simplicity debate, and relating its variance theory to Tan et al. It adds corresponding references alongside LiRA, RMIA, and GSAM literature, making the novelty claim more specifically about sharpness-aware optimization.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, experimental narrative, and theoretical section are substantially rewritten around the variance explanation. Section 3 separates direct and shadow attacks; retained minority-alignment theory moves into the appendices with reorganized proofs. The LLM-usage appendix and conference-review header text are removed.

P2.justification: v4 reorganizes the original optimizer table into a main SAM/SGD table and an expanded appendix comparison, adds paired multimetric online/offline tables, and introduces a sixteen-panel log-log ROC figure. Figures 1–6 retain their graphical content, with limited caption and placement changes; Hessian and architecture tables are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Tables 2 and 4 and Figure 7 strengthen the empirical privacy conclusion through sample-calibrated attacks and low-FPR evaluation, addressing v3's reliance on direct attacks and aggregate accuracy. Research positioning is also more precise. The net gain is limited by the new theoretical claims: Corollary 5's LR/ROC argument requires a member-versus-nonmember variance ordering absent from its statement, so its guarantee is broader than the proof supports. The retained direct-attack table also loses its repetition-count disclosure.
